indigo-galaxy · exedev · 2026-11-25 01:23-01:52 UTC · Claude Code 2.1.331 · agents claude-opus-5-5, effort xhigh · feat/stall @ 7caf0a9 (PR branch feat/stall) · one take, unedited

stall_min ends a stuck team's run on time, live with four Opus 5.5 agents

A real four-agent team got the bundled example plus an eighth statement, digest, whose frozen test can never pass. It landed the seven real statements 2 min 50 s to 4 min 4 s after launch. After that no merge could be accepted. With stall_min 4 and a 60-minute budget, the gateway wrote state/STALLED 240.3 s of unpaused time after the last accepted merge. A 239.6-s pause in between was correctly left out of that count. wait-run.sh printed STALLED 2.3 s later, every work request was then refused, and 51.9 of the 60 minutes were never spent. On main before this change, the same team would have been held at work until the 60 minutes ran out. boss.sh unstall reopened the run, the agents stayed idle until boss.sh say all, and the run stalled again 240.9 s after the unstall. I found three problems around the feature (findings below). None is in the gateway's timing.

The take (29 min, one take, pauses over 2 s shortened)

Recorded with rec.sh at 164x50. The shell prompt carries the clock. watch.py is a viewer I wrote for the recording, not part of the harness. It redraws harness/boss.sh status, the raw state/stall_from, the merges and the last 17 lines of each agent's real tmux pane, cropped to 80 columns, and it marks a chapter at each accepted merge. The windows were 188 columns wide because another client attached to the session 20 s after launch (see the audit trail). The poster frame is the moment wait-run.sh printed STALLED. The final merge chapter (6:25) was added afterwards: watch.py saw landed.json reach 7 before merges.jsonl had the line, and exited first.

Findings

  1. 1. During a pause, the boss's stall clock keeps counting while it says it has stopped. While state/HALT existed, boss.sh status printed 1, 2, 3, 4 and finally "5 of 4 min without an accepted merge (stopped while paused)". The gateway itself correctly did not count the pause: the run stalled 240.3 s of unpaused time after the merge. board.py computes now minus state/stall_from, but the pause is moved out of stall_from only when boss.sh resume runs. A boss who reads "5 of 4" will expect a stall that is not coming. Fix: while HALT exists, subtract now minus HALT's ts. template/harness/board.py:51-53 (the pause is only given back at boss.sh:35-46)
  2. 2. A stall reopened with boss.sh unstall leaves no trace in report.py or offline_monitor.py. unstall moves state/STALLED to records/stalled.<ts>.json, and nothing reads that file. report.py and offline_monitor.py read only state/STALLED. This run's report shows a single STALLED at 01:48:19 and no unstall. SKILL.md step 7 says the page shows "every pause, removal, resume, stall". Pauses are read from records/halt.*.json (report.py:97); stalls need the same. template/harness/report.py:92-95, template/harness/offline_monitor.py:53-56, template/harness/boss.sh:48
  3. 3. After an unstall, the lead's time-left reminders never come back. remind.sh leaves its loop at the first STALLED ("run stalled; reminders stop"), and boss.sh unstall does not restart it. For the rest of a reopened run the lead gets no reminders. Small, but the runbook presents unstall as reopening the run. template/harness/remind.sh:6
  4. 4. An agent learns of the stall only when it reads a refusal, which can be minutes late. The three helpers stopped 37 to 113 s after STALLED. The lead took 365 s. It was inside one Bash call that ran for i in 1..5; do team wait 100 | grep -E 'time left|done on main|unread|PAUSE'; ... to wait for the boss to fix the test. team wait ends with status, which the gateway still answers with exit 0 after a stall, so the grep removed the STALLED line and nothing failed. It cost tokens only, because every work request was refused. After the reopening, the lead added STALL to its grep by itself. A fix: have status (and so team wait) exit non-zero once the run is over. template/harness/gateway.py:581-585, template/bin/team:103-106
  5. Observation (not a bug): the team saw the impossible statement at once. The lead marked digest BLOCKED ("test asserts two different digests; lead handles with boss") at 01:27:28, 2 minutes after launch, before any code was written. Nobody tried to game the test. Agents cannot reach the boss: team msg goes only to agents, so the lead left the problem in the board's notes, and boss.sh status does not show notes. So the team waited for a fix that only the boss could make, and the boss is not told. That is exactly the stuck case stall_min ends.

Not covered

  • The old behaviour was not run for an hour on main. It is cited from the code (E17).
  • The pause was injected by the boss through harness/hook.py (as the tests do), not caused by an agent.
  • A stall that comes while a merge is being checked (the gateway lets that merge answer first, gateway.py:544-548).
  • A stall combined with an interrupted run and launch.sh --resume (time down should not count, runstate.py:141).
  • A fractional stall_min, profiles other than sealed, teams other than four agents.
  • Agents landing filler to reset the clock. Nobody tried, and nothing but the check prevents it (design.md says so).
  • ./teardown.sh --archive of a stalled run (this run was stopped with a plain ./teardown.sh, files kept).

Audit trail

One take, 1741 s, 30 chapters plus one added afterwards (the final merge; see the screencast note). No take was discarded.

Nothing was typed by a person. I (the boss agent) drove every command with rec.sh run/type. A background script (tools/phase2.sh) typed the timed pause, resume and wait-run steps.

Prompts answered: harness/boss.sh trust answered Claude Code's folder-trust prompt in the four agent windows ("answered yes" x4). No other prompt appeared, and I answered none for the user.

Messages to the team (facts only): "The pause is cleared: it was a test the boss ran, not something any of you did. Carry on." and "The run is reopened. Carry on.". There was no coaching.

The pause was not an agent's doing. I fed one hard violation (curl http://example.com, session_id "boss-test-not-an-agent") to harness/hook.py for h3. It is recorded in actions.jsonl as h3's block and appears so in offline_monitor's "items flagged".

The door probe after the stall was mine: requests from ws/h3 at 01:39:46-47, logged under h3. The one "rejected" mr that offline_monitor and report.py count is this probe. My first attempt at it typed team without its path, so every command said "command not found" (visible at 16:33). It reached nothing and I re-ran it.

Window size: 20 s after launch, a client I did not start attached to tmux session demo-stall and resized every window to 188x66. It was probably the owner watching. Nothing was typed into the team from it as far as the records show. The panes in watch.py are therefore cropped.

Outside the take: tools/busylog.py captured each agent pane every 3 s (the busy marker "esc to interrupt"). A 1-s sampler logged state/stall_from, HALT and STALLED. Both only read.

Redaction: the agents' commit messages showed a generic no-reply address in a Co-Authored-By trailer. I masked all 9 occurrences in the cast with same-length *. No keys or tokens were found (grep for sk-ant, api key, bearer, ghp_, password; no ~/.ssh or ~/.claude paths).

Cleanup: ./teardown.sh printed "nothing from this run is still running". The loggers were stopped, and tmux has no demo-stall, proof-stall or proof-stall-rec. The scratch copy run-stall0 was deleted by its script. run-stall/ is kept (central.git, records, report.html).
